🇲🇽🌎 <u>THE SPANISH KING COMES TO PALACIO NACIONAL — ON MEXICO'S TERMS</u>

For the first time since AMLO took office, a Spanish monarch walks into Palacio Nacional. Felipe VI meets Sheinbaum today, seven years after his last visit and after Madrid spent years dodging AMLO's 2019 demand for an apology over the Conquest — a snub so deep the king wasn't even invited to Sheinbaum's 2024 inauguration. She says she'll explain "why for us it is a matter of dignity." In March, Felipe VI finally admitted the Conquest held "many abuses." The Crown moved first.

🇲🇽🇻🇪 <u>MEXICO ALREADY HAS RESCUERS READY FOR VENEZUELA</u>

Hours after two earthquakes — 7.1 and 7.5 — leveled buildings across Venezuela, killing 32 and injuring more than 700 with La Guaira declared a disaster zone, President Sheinbaum ordered the Foreign Ministry to ready rescue and health brigades. Foreign Minister Roberto Velasco said Mexico offers "full support" to the Venezuelan government and people: "Mexico is and will always be solidary." No conditions, no lecture about who governs Caracas — just help on the way.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>$82.5 BILLION HEADED FOR MEXICO'S DATA CENTERS</u>

Mexico is set to capture roughly $82.5 billion in data-center investment between 2026 and 2031 — cloud, AI and IoT infrastructure riding the nearshoring wave, per the Mexican Data Centers Association (MeXDC). The country runs ~160 centers today near 300 MW, with 70+ new builds pushing toward 1,500 MW by 2030. 72% sits in Querétaro.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>KEN SALAZAR'S REVENGE MEMOIR — LONG ON CLAIMS, SHORT ON PROOF</u>

Ken Salazar — the US ambassador who publicly attacked Mexico's judicial reform in 2024 — is now selling a memoir recycling evidence-free claims that AMLO feared what "El Mayo" Zambada might tell US justice. He offers no public proof, but does admit he saw an elected judiciary as a gift to the cartels — the very reform Mexico's voters approved. Book drops July 28.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>39 CASINO GROUPS UNDER THE MONEY-LAUNDERING MICROSCOPE</u>

39 casino and betting groups in Mexico are under joint scrutiny by Washington's OFAC and Mexico's own UIF for laundering narco money. In 2025 operators paid 74 billion pesos in taxes and ate 6 billion in fines. Seven houses already sanctioned — tied to the Sinaloa and Noreste cartels — and the list reaches Televisa, TV Azteca and Olegario Vázquez Aldir.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>MEXICO'S FRACKING REVIEW PUTS SOVEREIGNTY FIRST</u>

Mexico's expert committee on unconventional gas finished its first fracking analysis — weighing energy sovereignty, social justice and environmental harm. "We listen to those who oppose fracking," Sheinbaum said, stressing it's vital to "guarantee Mexico has its own energy sources." Gas burned for power is set to fall as energy independence is built.

🇲🇽🚆 <u>TRUCKER STRIKE CALLED OFF — DIALOGUE, NOT RIOT POLICE</u>

AMOTAC truckers had called a national strike across all 32 states for June 24. Instead of riot police, Sheinbaum's government sent García Harfuch and César Yáñez to the table and signed a roadmap on highway security. "We will abstain from the announced mobilizations," said AMOTAC's Rafael Ortíz.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>OPPOSITION TRIES TO MANUFACTURE ITSELF A PARTY</u>

Mexico's INE votes June 25 to grant national registration to four new parties — including "Somos México," the rebranded vehicle of the anti-AMLO "Marea Rosa" and Frente Cívico Nacional. After a process opened in Jan 2025, it logged 294,141 backers across 205 assemblies. Couldn't win at the ballot box, so it's manufacturing itself a fresh logo.

🌐🔥🇲🇽 While the Giants Fight, Mexico Multiplies: Its Share of US Imports Jumps to 16.9%

On June 22, Beijing blacklisted 10 US defense-linked firms and barred 46 more from government procurement — retaliation for the Pentagon adding 65 entities to its 1260H list. US–China trade has fallen to its lowest level since the 2009 crash. The world's two largest economies are decoupling in real time, and the supply chains are rerouting.

The data shows who gains. Mexico's share of US imports climbed from 13.8% to 16.9% in just the first two months of 2026. Washington demands Mexico slam the door on China — yet Mexico already set permanent 10–35% steel tariffs and duties on roughly 1,400 products on its own schedule, to protect domestic industry and jobs, not to obey an order.

Here's the hypocrisy: the US weaponizes "free trade" against everyone while lecturing Mexico about Chinese imports. Mexico's answer is sovereignty, not obedience — keep options open with every partner, take the nearshoring windfall, and refuse to become anyone's collateral. In a multipolar world, the country that multiplies its options is the one that wins.

🇲🇽🌐 Mexico Doesn't Wait: Sheinbaum Will Propose a 16-Year T-MEC Extension on Its Own Terms

On July 1, Mexico won't sit and wait for Washington's verdict. President Claudia Sheinbaum will sign a letter formally proposing a 16-year extension of the USMCA/T-MEC at the trilateral meeting. Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard was blunt: "July 1 marks the start of the review process, not the end of it." Mexico moved early — not because it's cornered, but to define the terms and kill the uncertainty Trump's tariff threats manufacture.

The math favors Mexico's calm. If any party refuses to extend, the treaty doesn't collapse — it automatically stays in force for 10 more years, and no one has filed the required six-month withdrawal notice. Despite Trump's 25% tariff theatrics, most US–Mexico trade still crosses the border tariff-free. The "worst case," Ebrard noted, is a decade of guaranteed access.

This is sovereignty as strategy: define your position before the other side defines it for you. Mexico negotiates from a $1.6-trillion trade bloc it helps anchor — while diversifying toward Europe, Asia and Latin America. Stability isn't granted from the north. Mexico is writing it down and proposing it first.
